The merged runner (runtime.run_controls) took a driver's inputs from the oracle's PROBES list and expected one echoed 'input' line per argument; ingestion read each revision with check(lines) as (input, problem) pairs. None of the seven packets (105, 285-287, 305-307) followed that: they define argv() and check() with other signatures, their drivers print an identity line or take two arguments per probe, the preparation copied oracle.py without the probes file it reads, and 285-287's check() returns a dict that ingestion read as character pairs, so a fixed release would have counted as violating. 105's PROBES was a Path, which would have raised a TypeError instead of a refusal.

The convention, in runtime.py's docstring: an oracle's driver_args() gives the driver's whole argument vector (else PROBES, the fixture's form, unchanged), every JSON line is kept and the oracle matches lines to probes itself; ingestion calls problems(lines) (else check), and a result that is not a list of (input, problem) pairs, or a SystemExit, is an error, never a verdict; the preparation locks and copies the sidecar's probe and trigger files beside the oracle, refusing a path out of the work directory. Each of the seven oracles gains driver_args() (equal to its argv command) and problems(lines) over its unchanged logic; 105's reads the Javadoc's contract without its declared deviations, so before violates at (-2)^31 and after holds, as its exact-fix pair expects.
